sections.heading: What Are Continuous Hinges and Why Do They Matter?
sections.body: Continuous hinges differ from standard butt hinges in one fundamental way: they span the entire height of a door rather than attaching at just two or three points. This full-length design spreads the mechanical load across the entire door edge, which significantly reduces stress on any single point of the frame or door panel. The result is a more stable, quieter door that is far less likely to warp, sag, or pull away from its frame over time. For commercial properties in Chantilly — where doors may open and close hundreds of times each day — this durability advantage is especially meaningful. Continuous hinges are commonly used on heavy glass doors, aluminum-framed entry doors, storefront systems, and institutional entryways. They are available in a range of materials including aluminum, stainless steel, and steel, allowing our team to match the right hinge to the door weight, traffic volume, and aesthetic requirements of your specific property. Choosing the correct continuous hinge is not simply a matter of picking the longest one available — it requires evaluating door thickness, material, frequency of use, and the surrounding frame construction.

sections.heading: Our Continuous Hinge Installation Process in Chantilly
sections.body: Our installation process begins with a thorough on-site assessment of your existing door system. Once we have a clear picture of the scope, we select the appropriate continuous hinge profile and material for your application. We align the door carefully before final fastening, checking the swing, clearance, and latch alignment at every stage. After installation, we test the door through multiple open-and-close cycles to confirm smooth, consistent operation. faq.q: Can continuous hinges be installed on existing glass or aluminum-framed doors?
faq.a: Yes. Continuous hinges are compatible with a wide range of door types including glass, aluminum, steel, and wood frames. Our technicians assess the existing door construction to confirm compatibility and select the appropriate hinge profile before proceeding.

faq.q: How do I know if my commercial door needs a continuous hinge rather than standard butt hinges?
faq.a: Doors that experience very high daily traffic, carry significant weight, or have a history of hinge failures or frame stress are strong candidates for continuous hinge upgrades. If your door is sagging, difficult to latch, or showing wear around existing hinge locations, a professional assessment can determine whether a continuous hinge is the right solution.
